Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

some background on the need, in case it helps explain the purpose: the current mixer has been dropping channels 3 and 7. the technician's repair estimate was $680, and there isn't a reliable timeline for that repair. the fundraising goal is to replace the mixer and make rehearsal time more affordable for young musicians. we haven't bought a new mixer yet, and don't say the repair happened or that a youth-hours program has already started. the money is intended for those two priorities; we don't have a split worked out between them. please don't claim one priority is fully funded or say what exact amount will go to each.

night details, maybe use just the relevant ones: doors opened at four. Mara Bell played a solo set first, then Juniper Lines played as a trio, then the student duo Theo Park and Noor Patel played. Noor sang; they did one original and one cover, but i don't have the song titles. the sets were short and the room stayed informal, with people talking between performances. eleven volunteers helped with setup, serving food, the door, and cleanup. it was in the Grange hall, not at the Lantern Room itself. the rain is a small detail, don't make it a dramatic story about weather, and don't imply that it affected attendance. there were about seventy guests, again approximate. No need to invent an agenda or describe what the performers wore.

we counted the money after the event. ticket and door income together was $1,280. the small silent auction brought in $620, and additional gifts brought in $740. those three amounts are gross receipts of $2,640. expenses were $515 for hall rental, food, and printing, leaving $2,125 in net proceeds. make the gross and net distinction clear if you include the figures. don't call the whole $2,640 net, and don't quietly leave out expenses while describing the proceeds. there isn't a more detailed breakdown of the $515. the figures are counted, but don't suggest the mixer has been ordered or that the final use of the proceeds has been decided between the two priorities.

there are a few quotes that can go in, if useful. keep the wording and who said it intact if you use them; don't blend them into a new quote. Elian Cruz, one of the organizers, said, “We want the room to stay loud without making the next generation pay full price.” Mara Bell said, “I played my first all-ages set here when I was sixteen, and somebody made space for me.” Noor Patel said, “I practiced the harmony on the bus all week.” One volunteer, whose name isn't in my notes, said, “The kettle was working harder than the PA.” Don't invent a name or job for that volunteer. It's fine to leave a quote out rather than force it in. The first quote explains the two-part purpose pretty neatly, but don't imply that Elian spoke on behalf of every organizer.

please include a numbered section of exactly three short items that lays out the three sources of gross receipts: ticket and door income, silent auction, and additional gifts. Include the amount for each and label the section clearly. The expenses can be explained in the paragraph before or after that section, but don't create a fourth numbered item or turn expenses into a fundraising source. It should still feel like an email, so use a few paragraphs around the list, not just a report made of bullets. Maybe thank the performers and the eleven volunteers as well as guests and supporters; don't add names for volunteers or list donors. don't say every guest donated or imply every donor attended. End simply, without a made-up promise, new campaign, or claim about what happened next.", "output": "Draft a warm, grounded community thank-you email of about 450–600 words for people connected with the Lantern Room Music Room’s Room to Hear fundraiser. Include a subject line. Thank guests, supporters, performers, and volunteers without implying that every donor attended or every guest donated. Keep the tone personal and modest, not like a press release, grant report, or sales pitch.

The fundraiser took place indoors at Alder Street Grange on Saturday, November 9, from 4 to 8 pm. It was cold and rainy outside. About 70 guests attended—keep this estimate approximate—and 11 volunteers helped with setup, food service, the door, and cleanup. The event was held at the Grange hall, not at the Lantern Room. Do not exaggerate its scale or suggest that the weather affected attendance.

Explain that the proceeds are intended for two specific purposes: replacing the Lantern Room’s digital mixer and making rehearsal hours more affordable for young musicians. The current mixer has been dropping channels 3 and 7. A technician estimated repairs at $680, with no reliable repair timeline. The new mixer has not been purchased, and the youth rehearsal hours have not yet started. No allocation between the two purposes has been decided, so don’t say either is fully funded or assign it a specific amount. Do not describe the funds as general operating support.

The evening featured Mara Bell playing a solo set, followed by Juniper Lines as a trio, and then the student duo Theo Park and Noor Patel. Noor sang. The duo performed one original and one cover; the song titles are not available. The sets were short, with an informal atmosphere and conversation between performances. Do not invent an agenda or details about performers’ clothing.

Include a clearly labeled numbered section with exactly three short items listing the sources of gross receipts and their amounts:
1. Ticket and door income: $1,280.
2. Silent auction: $620.
3. Additional gifts: $740.

These total $2,640 in gross receipts. Expenses were $515 for hall rental, food, and printing, leaving $2,125 in net proceeds. Make the distinction between gross receipts and net proceeds clear. Do not call $2,640 net, omit expenses while describing the proceeds, or invent a more detailed expense breakdown. The figures have been counted, but the proceeds have not been allocated between the two purposes.

Use any of the following quotations if they fit naturally. Preserve each quotation’s wording and attribution exactly, and do not combine or rewrite quotations:
- Elian Cruz, one of the organizers: “We want the room to stay loud without making the next generation pay full price.” Do not imply Elian spoke for all the organizers.
- Mara Bell: “I played my first all-ages set here when I was sixteen, and somebody made space for me.”
- Noor Patel: “I practiced the harmony on the bus all week.”
- An unnamed volunteer: “The kettle was working harder than the PA.” Do not invent the volunteer’s name or role. It is fine to omit any quote that does not fit naturally.

Explain the steps needed to produce a current map for local visitors and for the group to update later.

## Site and access

Merebank Wood is about 3.2 square kilometres on the edge of a fictional town. It includes oak and beech on higher ground, an alder strip beside the stream, a planted conifer block, and two open clearings. Several footpaths and an old north track cross the wood; features include bridges, benches, and information signs. The stream follows the eastern side and drains into a pond near the south entrance. Lower areas remain wet after rain. The west boundary meets private farmland, and a fenced restoration area inside the wood is closed to visitors.

The group has permission to survey public woodland paths and accessible ground only. Do not plan to cross the farm boundary or enter the fenced area.

## People, schedule, and equipment

Plan for five weeks, with fieldwork on Saturdays if weather allows. There are six volunteers, but usually only four can attend a session. Nobody has formal GIS training; one person has used QGIS a little, and another is experienced at keeping paper records. The group can borrow a laptop with QGIS installed and has two smartphones, one handheld GPS unit, a compass, measuring tapes, pencils, and clipboards. The phones use different mapping apps, and mobile signal is unreliable in the northern half of the wood.

The group can print the existing 2018 paper map, but does not know whether its woodland edges and minor paths are accurate. The extra-supplies budget is £180. Work within these limits; do not assume specialist equipment or a hired surveyor.

## Mapping aims and known uncertainties

The group hopes to record:
- Path routes and surfaces.
- Bridges and other small structures, signs, and benches.
- Broad woodland-cover types.
- Places where the ground is regularly wet.
- Obvious storm damage.
- Patches of rhododendron noticed by volunteers.

The rhododendron patches have not been measured, so their locations and sizes need to be checked rather than treated as established facts. The caretaker said, “the north track is still there, but the wet bit has shifted since last winter.” Treat this as a useful lead, not a verified location. Visitors have also reported confusion near the pond, but the group has not checked those reports.

The aim is not precise botanical classification, a full tree inventory, or a legally authoritative boundary survey. Use broad categories ordinary volunteers can recognize consistently, and provide a way to flag uncertainty.

## Plan to develop

Explain what to do before the first visit, how to divide tasks across the Saturdays, and what to do if rain, poor signal, or an absent volunteer changes the plan. Suggest practical pairs or small roles that can work when only four people attend. Avoid relying on one person to hold all the project information. Make the approach suitable for volunteers with limited field time and mixed confidence using maps.

Describe a simple, repeatable method for tracing paths and recording features. State what volunteers should write down and how to use the paper map alongside the GPS or phones. Explain how to record a location when devices disagree. Include safe ways to note wet ground and storm damage without leaving accessible routes or entering the closed restoration area. Suggest understandable woodland-cover categories and a method for recording rhododendron patches without overstating certainty. Explain how notes should distinguish direct observations from visitor reports and the caretaker’s comment.

Propose a short, plain-language data structure that can later be entered into QGIS. Suggest fields and understandable choices for each feature type, and explain how to transfer and check paper notes. The volunteer with QGIS experience can do the final entry, but another volunteer should be able to review it. Describe a simple way to compare repeated observations, find gaps or inconsistent names, and record uncertain positions; avoid complicated analysis. Include a check before sharing the map, since an incorrectly placed path or a wet area shown as certain could mislead visitors.

## Final materials and limitations

State what the final map and supporting notes should contain, how to show approximate information, and what limitations to disclose. Visitors should be able to understand the main paths and features without mistaking the map for a navigation or safety guarantee. Keep the plan grounded in the five-week schedule, available equipment, £180 limit, access restrictions, and uncertain 2018 map.
